correctness.summary: Starting from the exact two-branch parametrization in equations (16)-(19) of arXiv:2609.19890, the expansion in N^{-1} gives identical cubic boundary coefficients on both branches and reflected quartic coefficients K0+16u^3-24u^4. Exact symbolic substitution verifies the cancellations, while direct high-precision evaluation of the original formulas approaches the predicted phase constants. The branch-switch and integer-junction cases were checked separately.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The source paper states only the quadratic endpoint law with an O((1-g)^3) remainder. Searches for the exact cubic constant, quartic constants, endpoint Taylor or differentiability statements, comonotonicity asymptotics, and synonymous Spearman-rho/Gini-gamma boundary formulations did not find the higher-order result. The older rho-footrule optimizer literature is a residual risk because an unstated sufficiently general expansion there could imply parts of the calculation.

value.summary: The result identifies the first asymptotic order at which the countably many algebraic boundary pieces become visible. It upgrades the source's endpoint estimate by one universal order and then gives an explicit quartic phase law and complete cluster interval, revealing a concrete failure of fourth-order endpoint Taylor regularity.

limitations: The result is local to the rho-maximal boundary near g=1.
The phase law is asymptotic and does not replace the exact finite-parameter boundary formulas.
No regularity classification is claimed at every interior algebraic breakpoint.
No statement is made about empirical sampling distributions of Spearman's rho or Gini's gamma.
Equivalent higher-order consequences of older rho-footrule calculations remain a residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
